caption: Plan backup power for a community. This sample shares eight batteries across six hubs and shows supplied energy, priority-score gain and remaining gaps.
title: Power planner

caption: Set each hub's power needs. Edit phones and internet, refrigeration, cooling, lighting, solar capacity, expected occupancy and priority before calculating.
title: Hub power needs

caption: Make the assumptions visible. Adjust initial battery charge, reserve, efficiency, solar availability and load levels before calculating.
title: Battery assumptions

caption: Explore a shorter outage. Changing the duration to 12 hours recalculates battery assignments, energy coverage and the hourly power balance.
title: Recalculate an outage

caption: Get a clear answer when a request is impossible. A 60% minimum at every hub cannot be met with eight packs, so the app asks for more batteries, lower loads or a lower minimum.
title: Clear infeasibility

caption: Test the same battery plan in three conditions: the planned outage, 40% less solar, and a 12-hour longer outage with 15% more demand. The round-robin comparison uses the same resources and minimum.
title: Test three conditions

caption: See the reason for each assignment. The explanation shows the minimum packs needed and the priority-score loss from removing one pack, while keeping other assignments fixed.
title: Allocation reasons

caption: Inspect the hourly values behind the chart. The accessible table reports demand, supplied power, solar output and stored energy for each modeled hour.
title: Hourly energy table

caption: Use an optional Charlotte forecast from Open-Meteo. The app shows the snapshot date and retrieval time, retains attribution and recalculates with the selected weather. Hub values remain sample data.
title: Optional weather

caption: Keep a named plan in this browser. Save its inputs so you can open it later, change the assumptions and calculate again.
title: Save a plan

caption: Compare saved planning cases. These three sample plans were created through the app: a 24-hour storm, a 12-hour overnight outage and a 36-hour case without a minimum floor.
title: Reopen saved plans

caption: Take the plan with you. Export calculated inputs and results as JSON, create a CSV allocation table, copy plan data or print a report. The JSON preview makes the inputs inspectable.
title: Export and inspect

caption: Reopen the same plan from JSON. Inputs are checked, imported results are discarded and the app calculates fresh results. Clipboard export and pasted import were verified end to end.
title: Import and recalculate

caption: Know how the result works. Read the energy-balance rules, exact allocation method, data sources, privacy choices and practical limits before real use.
